name: Kissimmee Prairie Preserve
notes: Florida's first DarkSky park. The gate closes 15 minutes after sunset, so reserve a campsite or astronomy pad and check in with the ranger before dark; red lights only on the pads.

name: Hopkins Prairie
notes: Small Forest Service campground overlooking an open prairie, with vault toilets and no electricity. Come in from SR 19 via FR 86 and FR 111, since Google Maps' northern route doesn't work.

name: Lake Louisa State Park
notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving late must call 352-394-3969 for the gate code before closing.

name: Black Point Wildlife Drive
notes: Wide marsh views over the Indian River, but refuge roads are open sunrise to sunset only, so there is no night access.

name: Lake Eola Park
notes: City park that stays open until midnight. Good for the Moon, planets and bright satellite passes; the Milky Way is washed out.

name: Alexander Springs Recreation Area
notes: Forest Service campground beside the spring. Campers get 24-hour gate access with a code; day-use hours vary by season.

name: Juniper Springs Recreation Area
notes: Forest Service campground around the spring. Campers get 24-hour gate access with a code; the boardwalk is closed for renovation.

name: Silver Springs State Park
notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and the campground has its own entrance at 1425 NE 58th Ave. Campers arriving after sunset must call before 5 PM for the gate combination.

name: Wekiwa Springs State Park
notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset call 407-553-4383 for the gate combination. Day visitors need an entry reservation.

name: UCF Reflecting Pond
notes: Campus lawn by Millican Hall where UCF's Planetary Sciences Group has set up telescopes for Moon viewing; good for the Moon and planets, not the Milky Way. Visitors need an $8 virtual daily parking permit.

name: Moss Park
notes: County campground between Lake Hart and Lake Mary Jane. The park closes at 6 PM in winter and 8 PM in summer, so after dark it's campers only.

name: Lake Apopka Wildlife Drive
notes: One-way 11-mile drive open to cars Friday to Sunday and federal holidays. The gate takes vehicles 7 AM to 3 PM and everyone must be out by 5 PM, so there is no night access.

name: Blue Spring State Park
notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset call 386-775-3663 for the gate combination. A camping reservation doubles as the entry reservation.

name: Playalinda Beach
notes: The seashore is open 6 AM to 6 PM under normal hours and closes for some rocket launches, so there is no night access.

name: Jetty Park
notes: The park closes at 9 PM except to campground guests, who keep beach access and 24-hour pier access. Campers can stay overnight to watch launches from the beach or pier.

name: Sebastian Inlet State Park
notes: Open 24 hours with a staffed north ranger station, so no campsite is needed. Use the north-side lots; south-side beach access is closed during bridge construction.

name: Three Lakes WMA, Prairie Lakes Unit
seasonalNote: No camping during Prairie Lakes quota hunts
notes: Primitive campsites by Lake Jackson need a free FWC camping permit, plus a daily-use permit to enter. Come in from CR 523 via Prairie Lakes Rd, since the route from SR 60 doesn't go through.

name: Colt Creek State Park
notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset must call before 5 PM for the gate combination.

name: Withlacoochee River Park
notes: The St. Petersburg Astronomy Club's dark-sky site: astronomers camp on the open activity field on new-moon weekends, since the campground is shaded by oaks. The park is open dawn to dusk, so stay with a campsite.

name: Hillsborough River State Park
notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset must call before 5 PM for the gate combination.

name: Salt Springs Recreation Area
notes: The largest campground in the Ocala National Forest, and the only one with full RV hookups. Gates close in the evening (8 PM in summer), so check in early; there's no cell service.

name: Clearwater Lake Campground
notes: 42-site Forest Service campground with lakefront sites. Campers get 24-hour gate access with a code; day use ends at 4 PM.

name: Holder Mine Campground
notes: Improved state forest campground with electric sites, reserved through ReserveAmerica. Busy with hunters during archery and small-game seasons.

name: Lake Griffin State Park
notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset must call before 5 PM for the gate combination.

name: Kelly Park / Rock Springs
notes: County park that closes at 6 PM in winter and 8 PM in summer. After hours the waterfront is closed and campers must stay in the campground.

name: Trimble Park

name: Bill Frederick Park at Turkey Lake

name: Cranes Roost Park

name: Lighthouse Point Park

name: Manatee Hammock Campground

name: Lake Kissimmee State Park
seasonalNote: Campgrounds closed for renovation since February 2026
notes: The park closes at sundown, and its campgrounds are closed for renovation with no reopening date, so there is no night access for now.

name: Fisheating Creek Campground

name: Little Manatee River State Park
notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset must call before 5 PM for the gate combination.

name: Fort De Soto Park Campground

name: Railroad Park

name: Oak Mountain State Park

name: Papago Park

name: Pinnacle Mountain State Park

name: Sloan's Lake

name: Echo Lake

name: Table Rock
